summary.headline: Moneyview Q2 FY27 profit rose 16% QoQ to INR 201 crore; management guides FY27 PAT above INR 800 crore.
summary.overview: First earnings call as a listed company covered Q2 and H1 FY27. Disbursals rose 7% QoQ to INR 7,701 crore and managed AUM closed near INR 23,900 crore. Total income grew 8% QoQ to INR 1,146 crore and PAT rose 16% to INR 201 crore, with pre-tax margin widening from 21% to 23% of total income. Management said asset quality was stable, with September collection efficiency at 98.64% and October similar, and reiterated a full-year top-line growth target of around 40%.

segments.name: Platform / partnership business (LSP model)
segments.commentary: About 75% of loan capital comes from lending partners; about 17 partnerships live, with no single partner above 13%-14% of platform capital and the largest at 10%-11%. Management said partner margins rose about 7%-8% YoY, supporting revenue growth faster than AUM.

segments.name: Own NBFC
segments.commentary: Provides about 25% of capital. INR 250 crore of IPO proceeds was downstreamed to the NBFC in October 2026. Management said cost of capital is falling and the NBFC is one of the largest partners on the platform.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PAT expected to exceed INR 800 crore (profit growth above 100% on a normalised basis versus FY26), per CEO and CFO.
Full-year top-line growth targeted at at least around 40%.
Opex to income expected to keep improving in H2 FY27 and beyond, driven by collections, CAC and tech/AI efficiencies.
Credit cost target to stay within 5% of average AUM near term; management expects it at about 4.9% and to keep improving over the long term.
Ongoing ROE expected around 30% once IPO equity is deployed; margin of about 23.5% to be maintained and improved.
Rating upgrade discussions with agencies underway; further cost-of-borrowing reduction expected over the next year as the rating benefits flow through.
capex_capacity: INR 250 crore of IPO proceeds downstreamed into the NBFC in October 2026; balance of the INR 750 crore IPO money held at the platform.
Management does not plan to use IPO proceeds to repay debt; intends to lever the added NBFC equity to raise more debt.
Credit rating was upgraded last year from BBB to A- with positive outlook; management is in talks with agencies on a further upgrade.
demand_pricing: Management said the festive season shows strong momentum in disbursals, collections and operating efficiency, and expects current growth rates to continue.

Digital personal loans are projected to grow 26%-27% a year through FY31; digital share of unsecured personal loans was about 15% in FY26. Personal loan market expected at INR 33-36 lakh crore by FY31 (industry estimate).

New customers: about 75% are sourced directly (roughly half organic, half paid marketing) and about 25% via embedded journeys with large consumer internet partners such as Airtel, Supermoney, PhonePe and CRED.
Partnerships contribute about 20%-25% of new business and about 10%-12% of total disbursals, per CFO.
About 65% of AUM comes from repeat customers; over 14-15 crore registered users, mostly tier 2 and tier 3 cities.

qa_highlights.question: How will FY27 shape up given H1 PAT of about INR 375 crore, and what are asset quality trends including bounce rates and 30+ DPD in Q2 and October?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects FY27 PAT above INR 800 crore. September collection efficiency was 98.64%, October similar; Stage 1 at 94.6%, stable QoQ. Bounce rate and 30+ DPD numbers were not given in detail.

qa_highlights.question: Will the IPO capital be reflected in NBFC capitalisation and when will rating benefits show?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 250 crore downstreamed to the NBFC in October; balance held at platform. Management is in talks with rating agencies; incremental borrowing cost is down about 2 pp to 12.7%-12.8% in H1 FY27 versus 14.5%-14.8% last year.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the lower cost of borrowing, will IPO proceeds repay debt, and what is sustainable ROE?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental borrowing is falling; average cost moved from 14.8% to 14%, expected to keep falling toward 12.5%-12.8%. IPO money will not repay debt but will support leverage. Normalised ROE rose from 29% to 31%; ongoing ROE expected near 30%.

qa_highlights.question: How are sourcing channels and partner concentration evolving, and does a rating upgrade help sourcing?
qa_highlights.answer: About 75% of new customers are direct and 25% from partners. Largest platform partner is 10%-11% (no partner above 13%-14%); about 17 partnerships live, adding 2-3 each year. Management said the rating upgrade helps influence partner cost of capital and sourcing.

qa_highlights.question: Why is revenue growing faster than AUM, and why did interest income lag AUM growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue reflects higher margin share from partners, with partner margins up about 7%-8% YoY. AUM growth in the last month of the quarter was not yet reflected in interest income; management also cited better customer quality as the cause.

qa_highlights.question: What is CAC trend and credit cost guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: CAC is 1.6% of disbursals versus 1.9%-2% earlier, with benefit from repeat and direct mix. Credit cost is targeted within 5% of average AUM; currently 4.9%, expected to hold near this level in the near term.

risks_watch: Credit cost at 4.9% annualised, up about 10 bps QoQ on annualisation; management targets staying under 5%.
Dependence on lending partners for about 75% of loan capital; diversification to add 2-3 partnerships a year needs to be tracked.
Rising competition for sourcing partners from mid-tier NBFCs, which may pressure partner margins.
Rating upgrade and cost of borrowing reduction timing remains uncertain; benefit flows to P&L gradually.
ROE optically diluted by IPO equity; normalised ROE to be watched as IPO capital is deployed.
Management did not disclose bounce rates or detailed 30+ DPD for Q1 and Q2; need to track in next quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, margins and profit outlook, with a clear FY27 PAT target. Cautious on asset quality, stating only that metrics are stable without giving bounce rate or 30+ DPD data. Some answers were deferred offline (opex split, partner-level data).
key_quotes: Given all of this, we believe that we'll probably going to exceed about INR 800 crores of PAT for the overall year.
It was a great quarter, both for the growth in our business and for expansion in our margins.
It is very stable from an asset quality standpoint.
We expect the ongoing ROEs to be kind of higher than that, somewhere closer to about 30%.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 top-line growth of at least around 40% and PAT above INR 800 crore, backed by festive-season momentum, partner margin gains (7-8% YoY), and falling borrowing costs, but no specific new capacity or order book was quantified; Q2 total income grew 8% QoQ and PAT 16% QoQ, with the 40% target implying a sharp acceleration.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Pre-tax margin rose from 21% to 23% of total income QoQ, opex/income fell to 34.5% from 35.9%, and management targets ~23.5% and further improvement; partner margins up 7-8% YoY and borrowing cost down about 2 pp.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Disbursals up 7% QoQ to INR 7,701 crore, festive-season momentum cited, and FY27 top-line growth guided at at least ~40%, though Q2 total income grew only 8% QoQ so the target implies acceleration.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capacity is discussed for a physical plant; capital is being used to lever the NBFC (INR 250 crore downstreamed, INR 750 crore IPO balance at platform), so a capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guides FY27 PAT above INR 800 crore versus H1 PAT of about INR 375 crore, which implies H2 of about INR 425 crore (roughly 13% above H1), and festive momentum is cited; upgrade depends on sustaining collections and disbursal growth.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Credit cost is 4.9% against a 5% ceiling and rose about 10 bps QoQ on annualisation; bounce and 30+ DPD data were not disclosed, and partner competition from mid-tier NBFCs may pressure margins.

rows.label: Opex-to-income keeps falling
rows.why: Opex/income fell to 34.5% in Q2 from 35.9% in Q1 and H1 is about 35% vs about 39% in H1 FY26; management expects further improvement from collections, CAC (now 1.6% of disbursals vs 1.9-2%) and tech/AI efficiency.

rows.label: Cost of borrowing reduction from rating upgrade
rows.why: Incremental borrowing cost is 12.7-12.8% in H1 FY27, down about 2 pp from 14.5-14.8%, with management expecting a further cut as the A- to higher rating upgrade talks conclude; average cost guided toward 12.5-12.8%.

rows.label: Ongoing ROE near 30% after IPO equity deployment
rows.why: Reported ROE of 27.9% is diluted by IPO equity; normalised ROE rose to about 31% from 29%, and management expects ongoing ROE near 30% once the INR 750 crore balance is deployed.

tone.note: Management was confident on the FY27 PAT above INR 800 crore target, margin around 23.5% and falling borrowing costs, but cautious on asset quality, giving no bounce rate or 30+ DPD data; analysts pushed on H1 PAT versus the FY target, revenue growing faster than AUM, and partner concentration.
